transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~70 minutes
Location: All-hands town hall (Zoom)
Attendees: Leadership + company-wide; approx 120 on call

Summary:
Elliot opens with a recalibration of the company north star and what success looks like for Q2; Marisol covers runtime and infra priorities; Priya walks roadmap shifts; Jonah and Ava address capacity and incident/playbook changes; time for live questions and anonymous pulse. Action items captured and owners assigned.

Topics:
- North Star clarity and metrics (growth vs reliability vs unit economics)
- Prioritization framework and roadmap shifts
- Capacity planning: Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
- Incident response changes and on-call expectations
- Hiring and org rhythm; all-hands cadence changes

Action items (quick list): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Elliot Chen: Hey everyone - thanks for joining. Um, we wanted to keep this tight, 60, 70 minutes ish, we'll cover the north star and then open for Qs. Give me like... give me two minutes of context.
[00:20] Crowd noise / applause 
[00:30] Elliot Chen: Quick reminder — talk cards on slido are open, anonymous questions are fine. Marisol, kick us off on infra please.
[00:37] Marisol Vega: Yeah thanks Elliot. So, infra update — we've been focused on three things, um, kernel selection improvements, smarter routing, and the Dedicated throughput work. The kernel thing, uh, is mostly done for the 13B family but there's still a little drift on long context runs that cost us latency. We're shipping a micro-optimization mid next week.
[01:05] Jonah Brooks: To add — we've seen tail latency improve in staging by about 12 percent after the KV cache updates, but there's still variance when bursts hit cold nodes. We're, uh, instituting smoother pre-warm for Dedicated.
[01:22] Marisol Vega: Right, and that pre-warm ties into our autoscale policy changes — Ava will talk about the ops changes in a bit.
[01:30] Priya Nair: I'll jump in with product framing — the leadership ask for Q2 was: make inference predictable and economical. We're shifting some roadmap weight from features into delivery — meaning fewer new surface area launches, more work on reliability, SLAs, and developer experience.
[01:50] Elliot Chen: I'll be blunt — we need to reduce surprise for customers. That means clearer SLAs, better observability, and a pricing signal that matches what teams actually use.
[02:04] Audience question (anonymous): Can you explain what "pricing signal" means?
[02:09] Priya Nair: Yeah — so like, if a request pattern causes lots of small cold startups, we want customers to be able to understand the unit cost and be nudged toward more efficient patterns — via docs, SDK defaults, and batching recommendations. Not punitive, but informative.
[02:30] Elliot Chen: Exactly. And we will provide modeling tools to estimate cost per route.
[02:36] [A few people type in chat] 
[02:42] Marisol Vega: On the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff — we had a lot of internal talk. Hosted is great for rapid iteration and lower ops, Dedicated is for predictability and data isolation. The plan: make the migration path smoother by allowing pinning of model variants and a fallback policy that won't break customer SLAs.
[03:05] Jonah Brooks: We've prototyped a policy engine that routes to cheaper compatible variants when the primary is saturated — it's not perfect yet, still some semantic equivalence issues for certain prompt styles.
[03:20] Employee (Engineer): Is fallback going to change the output consistency?
[03:22] Marisol Vega: Short answer: sometimes. We'll put guardrails and a quality monitor that will auto-roll back if regression is detected. We're investing in evals and production canaries.
[03:35] Priya Nair: That's one reason product will focus on rollout tooling this quarter — canary, A/B, automatic rollback.
[03:42] Elliot Chen: Okay, quick finance note from Samir... actually Samir you're on People — maybe Jonah, do you want to give the hiring impact note?
[03:52] Jonah Brooks: Sure. We tightened hiring a little — we still hire aggressively for critical infra and product roles but we slowed some feature teams. The ask to engineering leads is to prioritize out of backlog and submit headcount justifications.
[04:10] Samir Kapoor: I'll add the people angle — our goal is to keep hiring momentum but be deliberate. We'll open a prioritization window where teams rank requests; I'll run a sync with managers next week.
[04:24] Elliot Chen: Great. Ava, incident playbook?
[04:28] Ava Martinez: Yes. We're rolling a revised playbook that clarifies on-call rotation, expected RTO windows for different severity classes, and a cleanup process post-incident. We'll do a dry-run with a small set of teams first.
[04:43] Elliot Chen: It was clear from January incidents we need better blameless postmortems and faster triage.
[04:49] [05:00] Elliot Chen: All right, moving to metrics — Priya?
[05:05] Priya Nair: Metrics focus: latency tail (p99), unit cost per token, successful request rate, and customer happiness (NPS/qual). We also want operational metrics: deploy success rate, mean time to detect. We'll publish a weekly dashboard for leadership and a lighter monthly summary for company-wide.
[05:28] Employee (Product): Will the weekly dashboard be public across company?
[05:30] Priya Nair: Yes — limited to high level numbers. We'll avoid raw PII.
[05:36] [06:00] Elliot Chen: Quick callout — regional expansion. We're starting a pilot in eu-west-2 region for Dedicated customers to handle data residency asks. Marisol?
[06:12] Marisol Vega: EU pilot will have a private control-plane option and KMS integration. It's initially on a small fleet of nodes to test latency and runbooks. If you have compliance customers, flag them to solutions so we can include them in the pilot.
[06:30] Employee question (HR): Is there any change to remote work policy?
[06:34] Samir Kapoor: No changes now — but we'll start monthly office hours in major regions and an optional in-person summit later in the year.
[06:42] [07:00] Anonymous question: How are we measuring success against the new north star?
[07:04] Elliot Chen: We'll define a short list of leading indicators: sustained p99 under target, reduction in cost per 1M tokens for typical workloads, and retention of key enterprise customers. We'll iterate on those.
[07:20] Priya Nair: We'll publish a one-page north star doc with those metrics and alignment to teams.
[07:30] [10:00] Elliot Chen: Ok folks, a little bit about cadence — all-hands will shift to a monthly rhythm with a deeper quarterly leadership review. We'll keep the company pulse and a mid-month skip-level office hour.
[10:20] Leo Zhang: Ops note — we'll centralize project trackers so PMs and Eng leads can get a single source of truth. Expect an invite to the project-tracker training early next week.
[10:35] [12:00] Crowd chat: +1 on consolidated trackers
[12:10] Priya Nair: Roadmap changes — delaying public SDK feature X to prioritize performance for embeddings and generation. We'll surface a deprecation path.
[12:26] Employee (Engineer): Any guidance on backwards compatibility?
[12:29] Priya Nair: We'll keep semantic compatibility for 90% of calls; for breaking changes we'll give a 60-day notice and migration tooling.
[12:40] [15:00] Elliot Chen: Finance & pricing — we want to test a new tiering model on a small group of customers mid-Q2. It's experimental; we'll use it to understand elasticity.
[15:20] Marisol Vega: We'll only A/B test on non-critical traffic and provide safeguards.
[15:28] Employee (Sales): Will this impact AE commissions?
[15:31] Elliot Chen: We'll coordinate with Sales leadership separately, but the goal is to better communicate cost and reduce sticker shock.
[15:38] [20:00] Town hall polls: 72% approve of north star direction; 18% neutral; 10% concerned about hiring pace
[20:15] Elliot Chen: Thanks for the feedback. On hiring — we hear you. We'll be transparent about which teams are prioritized.
[20:25] Priya Nair: Quick plug — product will run a brown bag next Tuesday to walk through the prioritization rubric. Join if you're curious.
[20:36] [25:00] Live Q&A:
[25:05] Employee (Customer Success): Customers are asking for better traceability of requests for audits — is audit logging getting bumped?
[25:13] Ava Martinez: No, audit logging is still in scope; we're investing in log retention and access controls for Private deployments and Dedicated customers with compliance needs.
[25:30] Employee (Engineer): Are we open sourcing any of the evaluation harness?
[25:35] Marisol Vega: We're evaluating what to open source; some internal tooling will stay private for now, but we plan to publish sanitized benchmarks and a reference harness later this year.
[25:50] [30:00] Anonymous: Will there be more transparency on customer escalations?
[30:05] Elliot Chen: We'll create a lightweight summary that communicates trends without naming customers; privacy preserved.
[30:12] [35:00] Rapid-fire updates from leaders:
[35:05] Jonah Brooks: Hiring: two infra ICs joining in March; we're backfilling on the serving runtime team.
[35:18] Priya Nair: Product: focusing on rollout tooling and a few key SDK improvements.
[35:30] Marisol Vega: Research: pairing with applied ML on quantization profiles to reduce memory footprint on large models.
[35:42] Samir Kapoor: People: updates to parental leave and manager training rolled out next month.
[35:50] [40:00] Elliot Chen: All right — I'll close with context. We're shifting from feature velocity to reliable delivery. This is temporary emphasis until we hit the economics we're targeting. We'll measure progress publicly and iterate.
[40:20] Audience applause / reactions
[40:30] Elliot Chen: Final: we will follow up with the north star doc, the planning templates, and the incident dry-run schedule. Please fill out the pulse.
[40:45] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone. Quick reminder to check the roadmap doc and leave comments.
[41:00] Meeting close, folks linger in breakout rooms and small groups for deeper questions.

End of transcript.
